recommendations.title: Review team capacity
recommendations.description: Compare the planned workload with the team's real capacity and agree what can move or stop.

recommendations.title: Review workload distribution
recommendations.description: Check whether work is concentrated on a few people and rebalance it.

recommendations.title: Build psychological safety
recommendations.description: Make it routine to raise problems early, for example with blameless reviews, and respond to concerns visibly.

recommendations.title: Review planning practice
recommendations.description: Compare past plans with outcomes and adjust how work is sized and committed.

recommendations.title: Limit work in progress
recommendations.description: Agree a limit on parallel work and finish work before starting more.

recommendations.title: Reduce reliance on heroic effort
recommendations.description: Find out why extra effort is needed and fix the cause, so delivery does not depend on it.

recommendations.title: Improve release practice
recommendations.description: Review recent rollbacks and urgent fixes and strengthen checks before release.

recommendations.title: Reduce key-person dependency
recommendations.description: Spread critical knowledge across more than one person, for example through pairing and documentation.

recommendations.title: Strengthen test automation
recommendations.description: Add automated tests where changes are riskiest and keep them fast and reliable.

recommendations.title: Stabilize production
recommendations.description: Review the recent incidents, fix the repeating causes and agree how to prevent them.

recommendations.title: Improve observability
recommendations.description: Improve monitoring and logging so problems are found and understood quickly.

recommendations.title: Delegate decisions
recommendations.description: Agree which decisions the team can take without approval and make it explicit.

recommendations.title: Clarify decision rights
recommendations.description: Write down who decides what, and review decisions that waited the longest.

recommendations.title: Review leadership capacity
recommendations.description: Look at the leader's commitments and direct reports and decide what to hand over or add support for.

recommendations.title: Plan succession coverage
recommendations.description: Name who covers critical leadership duties and prepare them.

recommendations.title: Review the operating model
recommendations.description: Look at how work is organized across teams and agree changes that make it sustainable.

recommendations.title: Close the gap between delivery and technical resilience
recommendations.description: Delivery is strong compared with technical resilience. Invest in the technical foundations before the gap turns into incidents.

TH-001.name: Team burnout risk
TH-001.description: Heavy workload together with an unsustainable pace.
TH-001.explanation: The workload was reported as too heavy and the pace as unsustainable, a combination that tends to precede attrition and quality problems. This describes working conditions, not any individual.

TH-002.name: Low psychological safety
TH-002.description: People do not feel safe to speak up.
TH-002.explanation: People reported that it is not safe to raise concerns or disagree, which hides problems until they are expensive. This describes working conditions, not any individual.

DS-001.name: Chronic delivery unpredictability
DS-001.description: Commitments are rarely met and plans rarely match outcomes.
DS-001.explanation: Commitments were rarely delivered when planned and plans rarely matched what happened, so dates cannot be relied on. This describes working conditions, not any individual.

DS-003.name: Excessive work in progress
DS-003.description: The team works on too many things at once.
DS-003.explanation: The team reported working on too many things at once, which slows everything down and hides bottlenecks. This describes working conditions, not any individual.

DS-005.name: Delivery heroics
DS-005.description: Delivery depends on extra hours or heroic effort.
DS-005.explanation: Delivery was reported to depend on people regularly working extra hours or making heroic efforts, which is not repeatable and wears people out. This describes working conditions, not any individual.

DS-009.name: Release instability
DS-009.description: Many recent releases needed a rollback or an urgent fix.
DS-009.explanation: Seven or more of the last ten releases needed a rollback or an urgent fix, so releasing is risky. This describes working conditions, not any individual.

TR-003.name: Single point of failure
TR-003.description: A part of the system depends on one person.
TR-003.explanation: A part of the system was reported to be safely changeable by only one person. That is a risk to continuity, not a judgement of that person.

TR-004.name: Weak test automation
TR-004.description: Automated tests do not give confidence to change the system.
TR-004.explanation: Automated tests were reported to give little confidence to change the system, so changes are slow or risky. This describes working conditions, not any individual.

TR-005.name: Production instability
TR-005.explanation: Ten or more production incidents affected customers in the last quarter, so production is not stable. This describes working conditions, not any individual.

TR-006.name: Poor observability
TR-006.description: Problems are slow to detect and diagnose.
TR-006.explanation: The team reported that problems in production are slow to detect and diagnose. This describes working conditions, not any individual.

LL-001.name: Leadership bottleneck
LL-001.description: Decisions wait for a leader and the leader steps into team work.
LL-001.explanation: Decisions were reported to wait for a leader and the leader to step into work the team could do, so the leader has become a bottleneck. This describes working conditions, not any individual.

LL-004.name: Decision latency
LL-004.description: Decisions wait for a leader's approval.
LL-004.explanation: Decisions were reported to wait for a leader's approval almost always, which delays the work. This describes working conditions, not any individual.

LL-006.name: Leadership overload
LL-006.description: Leaders have little room and many direct reports.
LL-006.explanation: Leaders reported having little time for strategic work and people, together with twelve or more direct reports. This describes working conditions, not any individual.

LL-008.name: Weak succession coverage
LL-008.description: Critical leadership duties are not covered.
LL-008.explanation: It was reported that nobody could take over critical leadership duties if the leader were away. This describes working conditions, not any individual.

XD-001.name: Unsustainable delivery model
XD-001.description: Both team health and delivery stability are low.
XD-001.explanation: Team Health and Delivery Stability are both low before any deduction, so the way work is organized cannot continue as it is.

XD-008.name: Hero culture
XD-008.description: Delivery depends on heroic effort and on single people.
XD-008.explanation: Delivery was reported to rely on heroic effort and a part of the system on one person, a pattern in which results depend on a few people. This describes working conditions, not any individual.

TEAM_HEALTH.name: Team Health
TEAM_HEALTH.description: How healthy and sustainable the team environment is. 100 is healthy.

DELIVERY_STABILITY.name: Delivery Stability
DELIVERY_STABILITY.description: How predictable and sustainable delivery is. 100 is predictable.

TECHNICAL_RISK.name: Technical Risk
TECHNICAL_RISK.description: How well technical risk is controlled. 100 means low risk.

LEADERSHIP_LOAD.name: Leadership Load
LEADERSHIP_LOAD.description: How manageable the load on leaders is. 100 means a healthy load.

TEAM_SUSTAINABILITY.name: Team sustainability
TEAM_SUSTAINABILITY.description: How sustainable the team's pace is. 100 is fully sustainable.

WORKLOAD_MANAGEABILITY.name: Workload manageability
WORKLOAD_MANAGEABILITY.description: How manageable the workload is. 100 is very manageable; a low value means high workload pressure.

PSYCHOLOGICAL_SAFETY.name: Psychological safety
PSYCHOLOGICAL_SAFETY.description: How safe people feel to speak up. 100 is fully safe.

DELIVERY_PREDICTABILITY.name: Delivery predictability
DELIVERY_PREDICTABILITY.description: How often delivery matches the plan. 100 is always.

WIP_CONTROL.name: Control of work in progress
WIP_CONTROL.description: How well work in progress is kept in check. 100 means it is never excessive.

RELEASE_STABILITY.name: Release stability
RELEASE_STABILITY.description: How stable releases are. 100 means none of the last ten needed a rollback or urgent fix.

PLANNING_REALISM.name: Planning realism
PLANNING_REALISM.description: How closely plans match outcomes. 100 is a close match.

DELIVERY_WITHOUT_HEROICS.name: Delivery without heroics
DELIVERY_WITHOUT_HEROICS.description: Whether delivery avoids relying on heroic effort. 100 means it does; 0 means it depends on it.

PRODUCTION_STABILITY.name: Production stability
PRODUCTION_STABILITY.description: How stable production is. 100 means no customer-affecting incidents.

TEST_CONFIDENCE.name: Test confidence
TEST_CONFIDENCE.description: How much automated tests protect changes. 100 is full confidence.

OBSERVABILITY.name: Observability
OBSERVABILITY.description: How quickly problems are detected and diagnosed. 100 is very quickly.

KNOWLEDGE_SPREAD.name: Knowledge spread
KNOWLEDGE_SPREAD.description: Whether knowledge of the system is shared. 100 means it is; 0 means a part depends on one person.

DECISION_FLOW.name: Decision flow
DECISION_FLOW.description: How freely decisions flow without waiting for a leader. 100 means they never wait.

SPAN_MANAGEABILITY.name: Span manageability
SPAN_MANAGEABILITY.description: How manageable the number of direct reports is. 100 means none; a low value means very many.

DELEGATION.name: Delegation
DELEGATION.description: How well work is delegated. 100 means the leader rarely steps in.

LEADER_CAPACITY.name: Leadership capacity
LEADER_CAPACITY.description: How much room leaders have for strategic work and people. 100 is plenty.

SUCCESSION_COVERAGE.name: Succession coverage
SUCCESSION_COVERAGE.description: How well leadership duties are covered. 100 is fully covered.

TH01.name: Sustainable pace
TH01.description: Our team can keep up its current pace over the long term. (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree)

TH02.name: Workload
TH02.description: How heavy is the team's workload compared with what it can handle? (1 = very light, 5 = far too heavy)

TH03.name: Psychological safety
TH03.description: People on the team feel safe to raise concerns and to disagree. (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree)

TH04.name: Collaboration
TH04.description: The team collaborates well across roles and with other teams. (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree)

TH05.name: Role clarity
TH05.description: Everyone on the team knows what they are responsible for. (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree)

DS01.name: Commitments met
DS01.description: How often are planned commitments delivered when planned? (ALWAYS, OFTEN, SOMETIMES, RARELY or NEVER)

DS02.name: Work in progress
DS02.description: How often is the team working on too many things at once? (1 = never, 5 = constantly)

DS03.name: Release stability
DS03.description: How many of the last ten releases needed a rollback or an urgent fix? (0 to 10)

DS04.name: Realistic planning
DS04.description: Estimates and plans match what actually happens. (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree)

DS05.name: Delivery without heroics
DS05.description: Does delivery depend on people regularly working extra hours or making heroic efforts? (yes or no)

TR01.name: Customer-affecting incidents
TR01.description: How many production incidents affected customers in the last quarter? (0 to 20; more counts as 20)

TR02.name: Test confidence
TR02.description: Automated tests give the team confidence to change the system. (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree)

TR03.name: Observability
TR03.description: The team can quickly detect and diagnose problems in production. (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree)

TR04.name: Technical debt
TR04.description: How much does technical debt slow the team down? (1 = not at all, 5 = severely)

TR05.name: Knowledge spread
TR05.description: Is there a part of the system that only one person can safely change? (yes or no)

LL01.name: Decisions waiting
LL01.description: How often do decisions wait for a leader's approval? (1 = rarely, 5 = almost always)

LL02.name: Span of control
LL02.description: How many people report directly to the leader? (0 to 20; more counts as 20)

LL03.name: Delegation
LL03.description: How often does the leader step in to do work the team could do? (1 = rarely, 5 = constantly)

LL04.name: Leadership capacity
LL04.description: Leaders have time for strategic work and for their people. (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree)

LL05.name: Succession
LL05.description: Someone could take over critical leadership duties if the leader were away. (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree)
